Incentives

Understanding solar and battery incentives in Australia

What small-scale technology certificates are, how the federal battery program changed in May 2026, and the traps to avoid when comparing quotes.

Published 20 September 2026Updated 15 October 20269 min readSolvanta Energy editorial

Australian solar incentives are not a government cheque that arrives in the post. They are certificates, created when an eligible system is installed and then traded. In practice, the installer calculates the certificates your system earns, subtracts their value from your invoice, and handles the paperwork. That single mechanism explains most of what follows.

Step one: small-scale technology certificates

The Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme issues small-scale technology certificates (STCs) for eligible installations. For solar panels, the number of certificates depends on the system's capacity, its zone rating (which reflects how much sun your region receives) and the remaining deeming period — the number of years left until the scheme's scheduled end in 2030.

Because the deeming period shortens every year, the same size system earns fewer certificates over time. That is a structural reason why waiting is rarely rewarded.

Step two: support for home batteries

The Cheaper Home Batteries Program extends certificate-based support to eligible battery installations. From 1 May 2026, the certificate factor tapers according to how much capacity is installed:

Cheaper Home Batteries Program — capacity taper from 1 May 2026
Installed capacity bandSTC factor applied
0 to 14 kWh (inclusive)100%
Above 14 to 28 kWh (inclusive)60%
Above 28 to 50 kWh (inclusive)15%

Installation date, not contract date

The regulator has stated that rebates are determined by the installation date, not when a contract is signed — and has warned retailers against promising installations before a rule change unless they are certain the work can be completed in time. If a quote depends on beating a deadline, get that in writing with the consequences spelled out.

Step three: what your state or territory adds

State and territory programs are where most of the variation lives. Some are rebates with income and property tests, some are interest-free loans, and some are targeted at specific groups. Programs close, reopen and change their values, and a program that was available last year may not accept applications now — Victoria's interest-free battery loan, for example, is closed to new applications, even though the state's solar panel rebate remains available to eligible households.

This is why we link to the official page for each jurisdiction rather than a summary: a summary is out of date the moment the rules change.

The eligibility factors that actually matter

  1. Ownership and occupancy — many programs are limited to owner-occupiers, with separate categories for rentals or apartments.
  2. Household income and property value thresholds, where the program applies them.
  3. Whether the address has previously received support for the same technology.
  4. Whether the products are on the program's eligible product list.
  5. Whether the installer is accredited and engaged through an approved retailer.
  6. Whether the required documentation and photographs are submitted correctly.

Five traps when comparing quotes

  1. A quoted discount that assumes a certificate price the retailer has not locked in.
  2. A total price that only holds if you complete a portal application by a deadline nobody has explained.
  3. Battery capacity quoted as nameplate kWh while the support calculation uses eligible capacity after the taper.
  4. Savings figures presented without stating the assumed usage rate, feed-in tariff or self-consumption.
  5. Claims that you 'definitely qualify' — no installer can make that determination; the program administrator does.

None of this means incentives are not worth pursuing. It means the quote you compare should show the specification, the assumptions, the incentive treatment and the conditions in writing — and it should tell you what happens if the incentive value changes before your installation is completed.

Key takeaways

  • STCs are certificates created at installation and discounted from the invoice — not cash payments to you.
  • The deeming period shortens each year, so the same panels earn fewer certificates the longer you wait.
  • From 1 May 2026, battery support tapers by capacity and depends on the installation date, not the contract date.
  • State and territory programs vary widely and can close — verify against the official page, never a summary.
  • No installer can promise eligibility; the program administrator decides.
